# Background Extension

<!-- Generated by generate-swiftui-skill.py; edit the library sources. -->

Category: Layout

On iOS 26 and macOS 26, backgroundExtensionEffect fills available safe-area space with blurred, mirrored copies of a view. Apply it to background content before overlaying text or controls, so those stay sharp and unduplicated. Inspired by Enid (@ios_dev_alb).

- Before: Background stops at the safe area
- After: Mirrored background fills the edges

APIs: `backgroundExtensionEffect`, `safeAreaPadding`, `NavigationSplitView`

## Complete improved example

Adapt the behavior to the app; demonstration controls and values are illustrative.

```swift
import SwiftUI

struct BackgroundExtensionDoExample: View {
    @State private var phase = 0
    var body: some View {
        VStack {
            BackgroundExtensionDoContent(phase: phase)
                .frame(width: 280, height: 160)
            Button("Change safe-area inset") { phase += 1 }
        }
        .padding()
    }
}

struct BackgroundExtensionDoContent: View {
    let phase: Int

    var body: some View {
        if #available(iOS 26, macOS 26, *) {
            // excerpt:start
            LinearGradient(colors: [.cyan, .blue, .indigo],
                           startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                .overlay {
                    Image(systemName: "mountain.2.fill")
                        .font(.largeTitle)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.7))
                }
                .backgroundExtensionEffect()
                .overlay(alignment: .bottom) {
                    Text("Explore").foregroundStyle(.white).padding(8)
                }
                // Simulates the safe area supplied by a screen or sidebar.
                .safeAreaPadding(.horizontal, phase.isMultiple(of: 2) ? 20 : 40)
            // excerpt:end
        } else {
            Text("Requires iOS 26 or macOS 26")
        }
    }
}
```
